data.title: Top Video Game Stock Stories This Week, 9/11/26
data.description:
Nintendo (NTDOF) had a huge week with fresh Switch 2 news. Sony (SONY) also kicked off a big fall run. Additionally, Capcom (CCOEF) had a new hit game, while EA could soon see an even bigger deal take shape.

1. Nintendo Unveils More Switch 2 Games

Nintendo put on a big Direct show for Switch 2. The event brought news on Metroid Ravenous and Kirby and the World Beyond. Monster Hunter Wilds will also launch on Dec. 4. Final Fantasy VII Revelation is also coming to the system.

2. Saudi PIF May Merge EA With Savvy

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund may have more plans for Electronic Arts. Reports say PIF is looking to merge EA with Savvy Games Group. The move would put both firms under one large game group. It could be a major shift in the game space.

3. Marvel's Wolverine Leads Sony's Fall Slate

Sony is set to launch Marvel's Wolverine on Sept. 15. The new game comes from Insomniac Games. It will lead a busy fall slate for PlayStation. The game also faces a packed run of big new titles coming out later this year. However, Sony also had a falling out with Kojima Productions this week.

4. Control: Resonance Gets a Deep Look

Remedy Entertainment showed off more of Control: Resonance. The game is set to launch on Sept. 24. The new game moves out of the Oldest House and into a strange New York for a more open world compared to the first title.

5. Onimusha: Way of the Sword Hits Stores

Capcom launched Onimusha: Way of the Sword on Sept. 4. The game brings back the old Onimusha name but with faster swordplay. It is set in a dark take on old Kyoto. Early fan and press buzz has been good, with 1 million units already sold.

data.title: Eli Lilly Stock (LLY) in Focus as Company Completes $3.8 Billion AtaiBeckley Purchase
data.description:
U.S. pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly (LLY) has announced that it completed its acquisition of AtaiBeckley, a biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for mental health conditions. The deal is valued at $3.8 billion and provides Eli Lilly therapies for the treatment of clinical depression and other mental health conditions.

Eli Lilly has said that the acquisition of AtaiBeckley should boost its neuroscience portfolio. Eli Lilly agreed to pay $6.75 per share in cash for AtaiBeckley earlier this year, representing $2.8 billion. An additional payment of about $1 billion could be paid by Eli Lilly if AtaiBeckley reaches certain clinical trial, regulatory, and commercialization milestones, bringing the transactions total potential value to $3.8 billion.

Eli Lily's Growth Strategy

The purchase of AtaiBeckley continues Eli Lilly's strategy of growing through acquisitions. The company has been building its pipeline of potential new drugs by acquiring smaller pharmaceutical companies and biotechnology startups. Eli Lilly has spent about $35 billion on corporate buyouts and acquisitions since 2020.

data.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman Says Company Willing to Slow AI Development
data.description:
Responding to a growing backlash, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has told employees that the startup company is willing to slow its artificial intelligence (AI) development. Speaking at a company meeting, Altman reportedly said that the firm ‌is open to slowing development of its AI systems. The comments come amid rising concerns about the safety ​of AI and a public backlash to data centers.

Altman told staff that the ChatGPT maker could slow its pace of development to match other AI companies. Earlier in the week, several ⁠AI researchers issued stark warnings about the dangers of AI technologies. Jacob Coxon, a former OpenAI researcher, publicly accused the company of racing ​toward AI advancements without acting ​responsibly.

Worse, Evan Hubinger, a safety researcher at OpenAI rival Anthropic, warned that AI is advancing so quickly tat there is a greater than 10% chance it "could kill all humans" within a decade.

Growing AI Worries

There have also been multiple reports of AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic breaking free of human control and acting independently, raising safety concerns and calls for government regulations. Anthropic also released a paper over the past week that warns AI could lead to mass unemployment that upends society by 2030.

In its bleakest forecast, Anthropic's economics team forecasts that AI technologies will lead to employment in the U.S. collapsing by 21.5%, the unemployment rate among white-collar workers rising to 17.9%, and joblessness across the entire American workforce hitting 11.9% by decade's end. Also, office wages will fall 11.5% and labor's share of national income will drop to 45% from 60%.

data.title: Oracle's Q1 Beat Has Analysts Bullish but Cautious on ORCL Stock. Is It a Buy?
data.description:
Oracle's (ORCL) fiscal first-quarter results came in ahead of Wall Street expectations, sending shares up 6% in premarket trading, but analysts are offering mixed views on the stock. Strong cloud growth and a sharp increase in remaining performance obligations (RPO) helped offset concerns around margins and cash flow.

Revenue rose 30% year-over-year to $19.34 billion, topping the $19.13 billion consensus estimate, while adjusted EPS came in at $1.92 versus expectations of $1.74.

OCI Growth Accelerates

The strongest part of the quarter was Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), where growth accelerated to 121% from 93% in the previous quarter. RPO, which represents contracted revenue yet to be recognized, reached $664 billion, up $209 billion year-over-year and above the $618 billion consensus estimate. Oracle also raised its FY27 revenue guidance to more than $90 billion, with management expecting OCI revenue growth of roughly 120%.

Promotion

ORCZ: built for a short position on ORCL

Barclays Sees Further Upside

Barclays analyst Raimo Lenschow raised his price target to $252 from $250 and maintained a Buy rating. Lenschow believes Oracle's growth has reached an inflection point and should accelerate further. He also highlighted the completion of Oracle's $20 billion at-the-market equity raise, which improves the company's funding position and addresses concerns around its large AI infrastructure investments.

Stifel Flags Margin Pressure

Stifel analyst Brad Reback took a more cautious view, cutting his price target to $200 from $220 while maintaining a Buy rating. Reback acknowledged the strong quarter and accelerating OCI growth but pointed to lower near-term gross margins. Still, he expects improving operating expenses and stronger OCI growth to support EPS expansion over the coming years.

RBC Maintains a Hold

RBC Capital analyst Rishi Jaluria lowered his price target on Oracle to $165 from $190 while maintaining a Hold rating. The firm acknowledged Oracle's strong Q1 results but remains cautious about lower margins and heavy infrastructure spending.

Oppenheimer Sees Financing Relief

Oppenheimer analyst Brian Schwartz reiterated a Buy rating and $275 price target, citing accelerating OCI growth, faster capacity delivery, and infrastructure demand continuing to exceed supply. He expects Oracle's leaner cost base to help offset AI-driven margin pressure.

However, Schwartz flagged persistent gross margin compression, normalized net-new RPO, and increasing reliance on customer prepayments. The completion of the ATM equity raise also helped ease financing concerns.

Is ORCL Stock a Good Buy?

On TipRanks, ORCL has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 21 Buys and four Hold ratings. The average Oracle price target of $257.76 implies 68.5% upside potential from current levels. Year-to-date, ORCL shares have dropped 20.8%.
data.author: Sheryl Sheth

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Up Today, 9/11/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are trading higher on Friday. The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100 are up 1.10% and 1.11%, respectively. U.S. equities opened in the green after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said the Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 3.4% year-over-year in August, unchanged from July and in line with expectations. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy items, rose 2.4%, below the estimate of 2.5%.

Lower oil prices are also supporting the market. Brent crude (BZ), the global oil benchmark, is down 2.99% to $104 per barrel.

Rate Hike Odds Jump as AI Stocks Lead Market Higher

However, the CPI data sent rate hike expectations higher. The odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting climbed to 85.6% from 72.4% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool. Higher rates can pressure equities by increasing borrowing costs and reducing the present value of future cash flows.

data.title: ORCL Stock: Barclays Lifts Price Target after Oracle's Q1 Beat, Says Growth Has 'Inflected'
data.description:
Oracle (ORCL) stock opened 2% higher at Friday's market open after the company beat Wall Street expectations on both revenue and earnings. Following the results, Barclays analyst Raimo Lenschow raised his price target from $250 to $252, saying the cloud and software giant's growth has "inflected and should continue to accelerate from here."

Lenschow is a four-star-rated analyst on TipRanks. He ranks #1,342 out of 12,502 Wall Street analysts tracked by the platform.

Oracle Reports 30% Revenue Growth

Oracle reported 30% fiscal first-quarter revenue growth to $19.34 billion, while adjusted earnings reached $1.92 per share. Cloud revenue jumped 62% to $11.61 billion, topping the $11.51 billion consensus estimate. Cloud infrastructure revenue more than doubled to $7.4 billion, also beating the $7.09 billion consensus estimate.

Promotion

ORCZ: built for a short position on ORCL

For fiscal 2027, Oracle now expects adjusted earnings of $8.10 per share and at least $90 billion in revenue.

Barclays Sees Oracle's Growth Accelerating Further

Lenschow said investors may be ready to take a fresh look at Oracle after the earnings report, pointing to stronger growth momentum and a better funding position. He also highlighted Oracle's completion of its $20 billion at-the-market (ATM) equity offering. With the offering now complete, the firm sees less uncertainty around how Oracle will fund its expansion.

He added that management did a good job addressing investor concerns about infrastructure delays and margins during the earnings report.

Stifel Cuts ORCL Price Target

Stifel's analyst Brad Reback reduced his price target to $200 from $220 but kept his Buy rating on ORCL stock. Reback called the quarter "strong" and highlighted management's decision to raise fiscal 2027 revenue guidance to more than $90 billion. According to Reback, the outlook implies roughly 120% growth for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).

While he expects gross margins to come under pressure in the near term, Reback believes the impact could be offset by faster OCI growth and better control of operating expenses over time.

Is Oracle a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

data.title: SpaceX Stock Forecast – Why SPCX Stock Is Rising and What William Blair Expects Next
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) is inching higher at Friday's open as its expanding AI compute business gives Wall Street another reason to stay bullish. In a new report today, William Blair analyst Louis DiPalma reiterated an Outperform rating on the stock after SpaceX secured another major AI compute agreement.

The new deal is worth about $1.11 billion per month, or roughly $13.3 billion on an annualized basis, starting December 1. Read more: SpaceX Rises on $1.1B-a-Month AI Deal. Is SPCX Becoming an AI Stock?

Why William Blair Remains Bullish on SpaceX

William Blair remains bullish on SpaceX because its AI compute business is signing large contracts as the company expands its infrastructure. DiPalma said the latest agreement is separate from the $6.7 billion six-month deal SpaceX disclosed during its August earnings call. He noted that SpaceX has now secured four compute agreements in the past four months worth more than $11 billion in annualized revenue each.

"Last night's deal is SpaceXAI's fourth compute agreement in the past four months that is greater than $11 billion in ARR," DiPalma said.

SpaceX previously announced a deal with Anthropic worth $1.25 billion per month. It also signed an agreement with Google (GOOGL) worth $920 million per month.

The growing AI business has increased DiPalma's confidence in SpaceX's revenue target. The company expects to reach a $100 billion annual recurring revenue run rate by the end of 2026.

"Bret Johnsen, SpaceX's chief financial officer, indicated that he has even more conviction now in achieving the $100 billion ARR target in December," DiPalma said.

SpaceX Targets 5 to 10 GW of AI Compute

SpaceX is planning a major expansion of its AI compute capacity. The company now targets 5 to 10 gigawatts by the end of 2027. Its previous goal was 2 gigawatts by the end of 2026.

DiPalma believes SpaceX has an advantage because it can deploy compute capacity faster than its peers. The company also has a close relationship with Nvidia (NVDA), which gives SpaceXAI priority access to GPUs. "SpaceX has benefited from its ability to deploy capacity much faster than peers," DiPalma said.

The company is also moving ahead with its Starship program. DiPalma expects Starship Flight 14 in late September. CEO Elon Musk previously said SpaceX could catch its Starship vehicle within the next couple of months. SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said the company now expects to achieve that milestone by the end of 2026.

Overall, SPCX has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on TipRanks, based on 26 Buys, six Holds, and three Sell ratings. The average SpaceX price target of $227.66 implies 54% upside potential from current levels.
